analysis.method: Existing nearest-rank summary and binomial order-statistic P95 intervals; no new percentile implementation.
limitations: Intervals are conditional on iid continuous observations; serial closed-loop dependence and host stationarity were not certified.
Phases are not randomized independent paired blocks; some report generation also occurred on the host. Differences cannot be attributed solely to waiting analyses.
Generator queue time is excluded from HTTP time. Generator has a separate PID; server also hosts low-volume coordination and monitoring.
The pool acquisition hook is SQLAlchemy-version-specific and includes creation; 30 requests per route warm up each phase before measurements.
Only I/O-gated synthetic inference is modeled. Real model CPU/GPU, SDK timeout behavior, capacity and production settings are not certified.
Light HTTP timeout remains 10 s. Analysis client allows 150 s only to support the deliberately held <=120 s test barrier.
No P99, optimization gain or universal responsiveness claim.

sampling: Per condition: 30 warmups/route, then 1000 measured requests/route at fixed concurrency five. P95 has about fifty upper-tail observations per route; no P99 inference. Binomial order-statistic intervals reused from the existing helper and explicitly conditional on IID. Conditions are exploratory, not randomized paired optimization blocks.

initial_attempt.description: History returned 403 because generated accounts were not friends. Application enforced the rule correctly. Added bidirectional fixture friendships, suppressed successful-request capture, and repeated the experiment in a new disposable database. No product authorization change.

findings.description: Pool releases and concurrent light-request completion were proved while provider threads waited. History/pull tails were slower than health; server and generator CPU/RSS and pool acquisition/loop lag are reported separately.
findings.recommendation: Investigate SQL/serialization and host scheduling with independent paired blocks before attributing differences or proposing optimization. No product bottleneck or speedup is inferred solely from these phases.
